topic: Operating practice, emergencies, Volunteer Monitors and HF operation (G2B, G2D; 22 pool questions)

questions.question: Which of the following is true concerning access to frequencies?

choices.A: Nets have priority
choices.B: QSOs in progress have priority
choices.C: Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency
choices.D: Contest operations should yield to non-contest use of frequencies

questions.answer: Except during emergencies, no amateur station has priority access to any frequency

questions.question: What is the first thing you should do if you are communicating with another amateur station and hear a station in distress break in?

choices.A: Inform your local emergency coordinator
choices.B: Acknowledge the station in distress and determine what assistance may be needed
choices.C: Immediately decrease power to avoid interfering with the station in distress

questions.answer: Acknowledge the station in distress and determine what assistance may be needed

questions.question: What is good amateur practice if propagation changes during a contact creating interference from other stations using the frequency?

choices.A: Advise the interfering stations that you are on the frequency and that you have priority
choices.B: Decrease power and continue to transmit
choices.C: Attempt to resolve the interference problem with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner

questions.answer: Attempt to resolve the interference problem with the other stations in a mutually acceptable manner

questions.question: When selecting a CW transmitting frequency, what minimum separation from other stations should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?

choices.A: 5 Hz to 50 Hz
choices.B: 150 Hz to 500 Hz
choices.C: 1 kHz to 3 kHz

questions.answer: 150 Hz to 500 Hz

questions.question: When selecting an SSB transmitting frequency, what minimum separation should be used to minimize interference to stations on adjacent frequencies?

choices.A: 5 Hz to 50 Hz
choices.B: 150 Hz to 500 Hz
choices.C: 2 kHz to 3 kHz

questions.answer: 2 kHz to 3 kHz

questions.question: How can you avoid harmful interference on an apparently clear frequency before calling CQ on CW or phone?

choices.A: Send “QRL?” on CW, followed by your call sign; or, if using phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign
choices.B: Listen for 2 minutes before calling CQ
choices.C: Send the letter “V” in Morse code several times and listen for a response, or say “test” several times and listen for a response
choices.D: Send “QSY” on CW or if using phone, announce “the frequency is in use,” then give your call sign and listen for a response

questions.answer: Send “QRL?” on CW, followed by your call sign; or, if using phone, ask if the frequency is in use, followed by your call sign

questions.question: Which of the following complies with commonly accepted amateur practice when choosing a frequency on which to initiate a call?

choices.A: Listen on the frequency for at least two minutes to be sure it is clear
choices.B: Identify your station by transmitting your call sign at least 3 times
choices.C: Follow the voluntary band plan

questions.answer: Follow the voluntary band plan

questions.question: What is the voluntary band plan restriction for US stations transmitting within the 48 contiguous states in the 50.1 MHz to 50.125 MHz band segment?

choices.A: Only contacts with stations not within the 48 contiguous states
choices.B: Only contacts with other stations within the 48 contiguous states
choices.C: Only digital contacts

questions.answer: Only contacts with stations not within the 48 contiguous states

questions.question: Who may be the control operator of an amateur station transmitting in RACES to assist relief operations during a disaster?

choices.A: Only a person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license
choices.B: Only a RACES net control operator
choices.C: A person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license or an appropriate government official
choices.D: Any control operator when normal communication systems are operational

questions.answer: Only a person holding an FCC-issued amateur operator license

questions.question: Which of the following is good amateur practice for net management?

choices.A: Always use multiple sets of phonetics during check-in
choices.B: Have a backup frequency in case of interference or poor conditions
choices.C: Transmit the full net roster at the beginning of every session

questions.answer: Have a backup frequency in case of interference or poor conditions

questions.question: How often may RACES training drills and tests be routinely conducted without special authorization?

choices.A: No more than 1 hour per month
choices.B: No more than 2 hours per month
choices.C: No more than 1 hour per week
choices.D: No more than 2 hours per week

questions.answer: No more than 1 hour per week

questions.question: What is the Volunteer Monitor Program?

choices.A: Amateur volunteers who are formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations
choices.B: Amateur volunteers who conduct amateur licensing examinations
choices.C: Amateur volunteers who conduct frequency coordination for amateur VHF repeaters
choices.D: Amateur volunteers who use their station equipment to help civil defense organizations in times of emergency

questions.answer: Amateur volunteers who are formally enlisted to monitor the airwaves for rules violations

questions.question: Which of the following are objectives of the Volunteer Monitor Program?

choices.A: To conduct efficient and orderly amateur licensing examinations
choices.B: To provide emergency and public safety communications
choices.C: To coordinate repeaters for efficient and orderly spectrum usage
choices.D: To encourage amateur radio operators to self-regulate and comply with the rules

questions.answer: To encourage amateur radio operators to self-regulate and comply with the rules

questions.question: What procedure may be used by Volunteer Monitors to localize a station whose continuous carrier is holding a repeater on in their area?

choices.A: Compare vertical and horizontal signal strengths on the input frequency
choices.B: Compare beam headings on the repeater input from their home locations with that of other Volunteer Monitors
choices.C: Compare signal strengths between the input and output of the repeater

questions.answer: Compare beam headings on the repeater input from their home locations with that of other Volunteer Monitors

questions.question: Which of the following describes an azimuthal projection map?

choices.A: A map that shows accurate land masses
choices.B: A map that shows true bearings and distances from a specific location
choices.C: A map that shows the angle at which an amateur satellite crosses the equator
choices.D: A map that shows the number of degrees longitude that an amateur satellite appears to move westward at the equator with each orbit

questions.answer: A map that shows true bearings and distances from a specific location

questions.question: Which of the following indicates that you are looking for an HF contact with any station?

choices.A: Sign your call sign once, followed by the words “listening for a call” -- if no answer, change frequency and repeat
choices.B: Say “QTC” followed by “this is” and your call sign -- if no answer, change frequency and repeat
choices.C: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” then your call sign a few times, then pause to listen, repeat as necessary
choices.D: Transmit an unmodulated carried for approximately 10 seconds, followed by “this is” and your call sign, and pause to listen -- repeat as necessary

questions.answer: Repeat “CQ” a few times, followed by “this is,” then your call sign a few times, then pause to listen, repeat as necessary

questions.question: How is a directional antenna pointed when making a “long-path” contact with another station?

choices.A: Toward the rising sun
choices.B: Along the gray line
choices.C: 180 degrees from the station’s short-path heading

questions.answer: 180 degrees from the station’s short-path heading

questions.question: Which of the following are examples of the NATO Phonetic Alphabet?

choices.A: Able, Baker, Charlie, Dog
choices.B: Adam, Boy, Charles, David
choices.C: America, Boston, Canada, Denmark

questions.answer: Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta

questions.question: Why do many amateurs keep a station log?

choices.A: The FCC requires a log of all international contacts
choices.B: The FCC requires a log of all international third-party traffic
choices.C: The log provides evidence of operation needed to renew a license without retest
choices.D: To help with a reply if the FCC requests information about your station

questions.answer: To help with a reply if the FCC requests information about your station

questions.question: Which of the following is required when participating in a contest on HF frequencies?

choices.A: Submit a log to the contest sponsor
choices.B: Send a QSL card to the stations worked, or QSL via Logbook of The World
choices.C: Identify your station according to normal FCC regulations

questions.answer: Identify your station according to normal FCC regulations

questions.question: What is QRP operation?

choices.A: Remote piloted model control
choices.B: Low-power transmit operation
choices.C: Transmission using Quick Response Protocol

questions.answer: Low-power transmit operation

questions.question: Why are signal reports typically exchanged at the beginning of an HF contact?

choices.A: To allow each station to operate according to conditions
choices.B: To be sure the contact will count for award programs
choices.C: To follow standard radiogram structure
choices.D: To allow each station to calibrate their frequency display

questions.answer: To allow each station to operate according to conditions
